businessModel: Free freeware; no business model documented
updateCadence: Irregular; a few releases a year, trailing Chrome by several milestones
summary: Cent Browser is a free Windows Chromium build from Cent Studio with mouse gestures, a scrollable tab bar and super drag. Its October 2026 release still supports Windows 7 and Manifest V2 extensions.
bestFor: Windows 7 and 8 users who want a recent-ish Chromium
People who like mouse gestures and drag tricks
Users who still rely on Manifest V2 extensions
notFor: People who need fast security updates
Anyone who wants an open-source or audited build

pros.title: Mouse gestures built in
pros.detail: Right-button gestures switch tabs, refresh or open history without an extension.

pros.title: Still supports Windows 7
pros.detail: The October 2026 changelog keeps Windows 7 support.

pros.title: Manifest V2 allowed
pros.detail: The changelog says MV2 extensions still work.

pros.title: Chrome extensions
pros.detail: Works with Chrome Web Store extensions; Google-account sync is supported.

cons.title: Lagging Chromium
cons.detail: Version 5.3 uses Chromium 150, several milestones behind Chrome.

cons.title: Closed source and opaque
cons.detail: Proprietary build with little published about the developer or telemetry.

cons.title: Irregular updates
cons.detail: Download sites note it is not updated as often as Chrome.

faq.a: It is a Chromium build, but it trails Chrome by several milestones and is closed source, so patch speed is a concern.

faq.q: Does it support Manifest V2 extensions?
faq.a: The October 2026 changelog says so; Chrome Web Store removed MV2 listings on 2026-08-31, so installs may need sideloading.

timeline.event: Version 5.3.1184.25 on Chromium 150, with Quick URL shortcut and selected-text translation

switching.note: Chromium import tools; Google sign-in syncs Chrome data.

spec.sandbox: Chromium sandbox (on legacy Windows may be weaker)
spec.patchLag: About 4 milestones behind Chrome by version number

jsSpeed: Chromium V8, a few milestones old
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox; legacy OS paths weaker
patchSpeed: Chromium 150 in Oct 2026, several milestones behind
